question: Select the correct order of Chlorine, Bromine and Iodine for Dobereiner's Law of Triads.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chlorine, Bromine, Iodine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Chlorine (Cl)**

 
 
• **Atomic Number:** 17 (meaning it has 17 protons in its nucleus).
 
• **Atomic Mass:** Approximately 35.453 amu (atomic mass units). This is an average atomic mass due to the existence of chlorine isotopes.
 
• **Electron Configuration:** [Ne] 3s² 3p⁵ (meaning it has 7 valence electrons in its outermost shell, making it highly reactive).
 
• **Group 17 Element:** Chlorine is a member of the halogen group (Group 17) on the periodic table.
 
• **Highly Reactive:** It's a highly reactive nonmetal, readily gaining an electron to achieve a stable octet configuration.
 
• **Diatomic Molecule:** In its elemental form, chlorine exists as a diatomic molecule (Cl₂), a greenish-yellow gas at room temperature.
 
• **Strong Oxidizing Agent:** Chlorine is a strong oxidizing agent, meaning it readily accepts electrons from other substances.
 
• **Disinfectant:** Due to its oxidizing properties, chlorine is widely used as a disinfectant in water treatment and swimming pools.
 
• **Industrial Uses:** It's also used in the production of various chemicals, plastics, and other industrial products.
 
• **Toxic Gas:** Chlorine gas is toxic and can be harmful to human health.
 
 
 
• **Bromine (Br)**
 
 
• **Atomic Number:** 35
 
• **Atomic Mass:** Approximately 79.904 amu.
 
• **Electron Configuration:** [Ar] 4s² 3d¹⁰ 4p⁵ (again, 7 valence electrons).
 
• **Halogen:** Bromine is also a halogen (Group 17).
 
• **Reactive Nonmetal:** It's a reactive nonmetal, although less reactive than chlorine.
 
• **Diatomic Molecule:** It exists as a diatomic molecule (Br₂) at room temperature, a reddish-brown liquid that readily vaporizes into a gas with an irritating odor.
 
• **Oxidizing Agent:** Bromine is also an oxidizing agent.
 
• **Uses:** It has various uses, including in the production of flame retardants, photographic film, and some pharmaceuticals.
 
• **Harmful:** Bromine is harmful and its vapors can be irritating to the eyes and respiratory system.
 
• **Naturally Occurring Isotopes:** Bromine has two naturally occurring stable isotopes.
 
 
 
• **Iodine (I)**
 
 
• **Atomic Number:** 53
 
• **Atomic Mass:** Approximately 126.904 amu.
 
• **Electron Configuration:** [Kr] 5s² 4d¹⁰ 5p⁵ (7 valence electrons, as expected for a halogen).
 
• **Halogen:** Iodine is the heaviest of the stable halogens.
 
• **Reactive (but less so):** It's reactive, but less so than chlorine or bromine.
 
• **Diatomic Molecule:** It exists as a diatomic molecule (I₂) at room temperature, a purple-black solid that sublimes into a violet gas.
 
• **Essential Nutrient:** Iodine is an essential nutrient for humans, particularly for thyroid hormone production.
 
• **Uses:** It's used in disinfectants, antiseptics, and in the production of some medications.
 
• **Iodine Deficiency:** Iodine deficiency can lead to various health problems.
 
• **Sublimation:** Iodine's ability to sublime (go directly from solid to gas) makes it visually interesting.
